title: Bangladeshi households are resilient through work and networks, but cumulative shocks are converting near-poverty into a fragile middle
source_unit: Power and Participation Research Centre, State of the Real Economy 2026: Dynamics of Reversals and Resilience in Bangladesh
geography: Bangladesh; nationally representative household survey conducted in 2025 with analysis of household economy, work, health, social protection, digital participation, and governance

observations.period: 2025 survey; household financial room, poverty, and vulnerable non-poor status

upper_poverty_line.unit: percent of surveyed households below the report's upper poverty line

budget_room.value: For many households, income is absorbed by essentials, leaving little room to save or absorb illness, price shocks, or income loss

fragile_middle.value: Poverty is only part of the story: households above the poverty line can remain near it and exposed to downward mobility

observations.method: PPRC nationally representative household survey and multidimensional analysis of income, expenditure, poverty, vulnerability, and household security.
observations.uncertainty: The report's poverty thresholds and vulnerability classification are survey- and methodology-dependent; cross-sectional status does not establish mobility, duration, or causal pathways into or out of poverty.
observations.subgroup: Poor households, vulnerable non-poor households, rural and urban households, workers, households with illness, and families with different income and asset positions.
observations.counterinterpretation: Limited budget room can coexist with adaptive strategies and informal support; vulnerable non-poor status identifies exposure to shocks, not inevitable impoverishment.

risk_stack.value: Informal work, debt, food insecurity, chronic illness, limited savings, inadequate protection, and governance frictions reinforce one another

recovery_difficulty.value: The accumulation of risks, rather than a single shock alone, makes household recovery difficult

health_finance.value: Health-related expenditure is identified as part of the economic-security problem alongside employment, debt, food, and social protection

governance_friction.value: Institutional harassment and governance frictions are included as household-economic pressures rather than treated as external political context

observations.method: PPRC survey analysis across employment, income, expenditure, savings, debt, food insecurity, chronic illness, social protection, institutional experience, and governance.
observations.uncertainty: The report identifies multidimensional co-occurrence and household perceptions; it does not by itself estimate causal interaction effects or compare the relative contribution of each pressure.
observations.subgroup: Households with informal or under-employed workers, debt exposure, food insecurity, chronic illness, weak savings, or limited access to protection and fair institutions.
observations.counterinterpretation: Multiple pressures can prompt effective diversification, migration, or mutual aid; correlation among risks does not prove that one domain causes the others.

observations.period: 2025 survey; household resilience, coping, and limits

coping_routes.value: Households adapt through work, migration, social networks, asset use, and other forms of adjustment

resilience_fragility.value: Persistent household resilience coexists with growing economic fragility and reversals in poverty reduction

institutional_limit.value: Coping mechanisms cannot substitute indefinitely for reliable institutions, productive work, social protection, health financing, and accountable governance

resilience_meaning.value: Resilience is treated as an active household practice with material costs, not proof that households are secure or that institutions are functioning well

observations.method: PPRC household survey synthesis and interpretation of work, migration, networks, assets, adaptation, and institutional support.
observations.uncertainty: Self-reported coping and cross-sectional resilience measures do not quantify depletion of assets, unpaid time, mental load, or the durability of adaptation after repeated shocks.
observations.subgroup: Households relying on labor diversification, migration, kin and community networks, assets, informal finance, or digital participation to manage shocks.
observations.counterinterpretation: Networks and migration may create durable mobility and opportunity rather than only emergency coping; institutional support can be effective even when household strategies remain necessary.

observations.period: 2026 report; transition compact and policy translation

denominator.unit: Bangladesh household-centered policy framework proposed by the report

policy_compact.value: The report proposes a transition compact linking productive employment, social protection, health financing, human-capital investment, digital capability, and accountable economic governance

peoples_lens.value: It asks whether major economic decisions reduce household risk, expand productive capability, protect dignity, and strengthen citizen voice

growth_security_gap.value: The report shifts evaluation from aggregate growth toward whether households gain security, capability, dignity, and voice

digital_inclusion.value: Digital participation and capability are treated as part of the household transition rather than as a separate technology sector

observations.method: PPRC synthesis of survey findings into a household-centered policy agenda and sequenced transition compact.
observations.uncertainty: The compact is a policy proposal, not evidence that implementation has occurred or that its components will produce the stated outcomes; priorities may not resolve trade-offs among fiscal cost, speed, coverage, and accountability.
observations.subgroup: Bangladeshi households, workers, social-protection recipients, health users, students, digitally excluded groups, citizens, and public institutions.
observations.counterinterpretation: Household-centered criteria can improve policy relevance but may underweight macroeconomic, ecological, or collective outcomes that are not immediately visible at household level.

related_sources.claim: Permanent DOI and citation record for the PPRC State of the Real Economy 2026 report.
Official PPRC report page with overview, findings, methodology links, and policy agenda.
Complementary World Bank country context for Bangladesh's development and household economy.

boundary: This record adds a comparative household-security route from poverty and near-poverty through budget room, cumulative shocks, informal work, debt, food insecurity, health costs, social protection, coping networks, digital participation, and accountable governance. It is based on a nationally representative Bangladesh household survey and policy synthesis; it does not establish causal effects, long-term mobility, cross-country equivalence, or that resilience means material security.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official PPRC State of the Real Economy 2026 page was reviewed for the 8,067-household nationally representative survey frame, poverty and vulnerable-non-poor shares, household budget room, cumulative risk stack, coping routes, institutional limits, and transition-compact policy framework.
